text: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991.
Key Features

• Readability: Uses clean syntax and significant whitespace indentation.
• Versatility: Supports multiple paradigms including object-oriented, functional, and procedural programming.
• Batteries-Included: Comes with a comprehensive standard library and an expansive ecosystem of third-party packages.
• Dynamic Typing: Manages memory automatically using reference counting and a cycle-detecting garbage collector.
Common Uses

• Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning: Powered by libraries such as TensorFlow, Keras, NumPy, and PyTorch.
• Web Development: Built with back-end frameworks like Django and Flask.
• Data Science & Analytics: Utilized via tools like Pandas and Matplotlib to process and visualize data.
• Automation & Scripting: Used to write scripts for system administration, testing, and file management
What Coding Is Used For

• Web Development: Building interactive websites and browser interfaces using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
• Software & App Creation: Developing mobile apps, desktop programs, and operating systems with languages like Python, Java, C++, Swift, and Kotlin.
• Data Analysis & AI: Processing massive datasets, automating workflows, and training machine learning models.
• Database Management: Storing, organizing, and querying data using SQL and backend frameworks.
Coding vs. Programming

• Coding: The specific act of writing lines of code in a chosen syntax.
• Programming: The larger umbrella of software development, which includes system architecture, algorithm design, testing, debugging, and long-term maintenance.
How to Get Started

1. Choose a beginner-friendly language: Python is widely recommended because it reads like plain English and supports web, data, and AI workflows. (Free interactive platforms like Coddy Tech offer step-by-step browser lessons).
2. Learn core concepts: Understand variables, loops, conditions, and functions.
3. Build small projects: Focus 70% of your time on building real-world projects rather than just reading theory.
Maternity leave in India is governed by the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 (and related provisions under the Code on Social Security), which applies to establishments with 10 or more employees.
Eligibility

• Work Requirement: You must have worked for your employer for at least 80 days in the 12 months preceding your expected date of delivery.
• Applicability: Covers women in factories, mines, plantations, shops, and corporate/private organizations.
Leave Duration

• First Two Children: 26 weeks of paid leave (up to 8 weeks can be taken before the expected delivery, and the remaining after).
• Third Child Onward: 12 weeks of paid leave (up to 6 weeks before delivery).
• Adoption or Surrogacy (Commissioning Mothers): 12 weeks of paid leave from the date the child is handed over (applicable if the adopted child is under 3 months old).
• Miscarriage or Medical Termination: 6 weeks of paid leave following the day of the miscarriage.
• Tubectomy Operation: 2 weeks of paid leave following the procedure.
Financial & Monetary Benefits

• Paid Leave: Full average daily wage paid by the employer for the entire duration of the leave.
• Medical Bonus: A statutory medical bonus (typically ₹3,500 or as prescribed) if the employer does not provide free pre-natal and post-natal medical care.
Workplace Rights & Amenities

• Job Security: It is illegal for an employer to dismiss, discharge, or demote a woman during or due to maternity leave.
• Crèche Facility: Establishments with 50 or more employees must provide crèche (daycare) facilities, allowing the mother up to four daily visits.
• Nursing Breaks: Two daily nursing breaks during work hours until the child reaches 15 months of age.
• Work-from-Home: Optional work-from-home arrangements may be allowed post-leave depending on the nature of the work and mutual
Choosing between GATE CSE (Computer Science and Engineering) and GATE DA (Data Science and Artificial Intelligence) depends on your academic background, career goals, and preferred subjects.
Syllabus Comparison

• GATE CSE: Focuses on core computer systems and theory. Subjects include Operating Systems, Computer Networks, Computer Organization & Architecture, Theory of Computation, Compiler Design, Digital Logic, DBMS, Algorithms, Data Structures, and basic Mathematics/Aptitude.
• GATE DA: Focuses heavily on mathematics, machine learning, and data handling. Subjects include Probability & Statistics, Linear Algebra, Calculus & Optimization, Python Programming, Data Structures, DBMS & Data Warehousing, Machine Learning, and Artificial Intelligence. It omits heavy core systems subjects like OS, Computer Networks, COA, and TOC.
• Overlap: Roughly 60% to 65% of the syllabus is shared between both papers (including general aptitude, basic programming/data structures, DBMS, and foundational linear algebra/probability).
